title: Goths
capsule: The Goths were an East Germanic people first attested in Roman records of the early third century CE, associated with a homeland on the lower Vistula (the 'Gothiscandza' of later legend) before their migration to the Pontic steppe region north of the Black Sea, where they appear from c. 230 onward. They raided across the Danube into Roman territory from the 250s, sacking Thessaloniki, ravaging Asia Minor, and killing the emperor Decius at Abritus in 251. By the late third century they had differentiated into the Visigoths (Therving) west of the Dniester and the Ostrogoths (Greuthung) east of it; the dataset closes at 207, capturing the early phase of steppe consolidation before the Roman raiding phase reached its height.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Goths in this early period were a mobile confederacy rather than a territorially defined polity; their steppe territory can only be approximately delineated from archaeological evidence (Wielbark/Chernyakhov cultures) and sparse Roman texts.
